detail: CHANNEL CREATED. Musa Ahmad joins #t (C084Y1ASX9A) at 16:20:48 GMT
Musa adds the "t" bot integration; the bot joins at 16:22:15
First bot interaction: musa types "ot", nobody accepts, bot orders a selfish tea
Alex Williams, Tim, Marcus, Jem, Sasha and Stephen all join within the same second
Early RNG bug: three-dice totals outside 3-18 (a 20 and a 1 in consecutive rounds)
Musa links github.com/musahmad/tea-bot for the first time
Alex: "needs a 'u up?' healthz check". Musa: "Should add it to grafana". Marcus: "tbot down?"
Marcus: "i think we should drop market making in favour of this ... i'm all in ... pivot". Also asks to push "t-statistics (pun intended)" to Atlas and whether tbot needs an org repo.

Alex Williams' day-one enhancement list: unique names, case-insensitive commands, re-roll, and per-person dice messages "like Jem: 4...6...2 ... builds the suspense". The per-die animation ships 2025-06-14; rerolls 2025-06-10.
Jem: "should use the dice emoji too like the unicode dice faces". Sasha: "you can strip whitespace too"
Musa adds the "t" integration (bot user U084VFPKR0S) to the channel
The brew timer is "quite fucked" - a deadlock in the Slack-update loop. Marcus code-reviews Musa's Rust: reuse the reqwest client, wrap it in an Arc, split the update and counting tasks
Musa: "This has been a good learning exercise ... I think I'm ready to do a market adapter". The tea bot was Musa's Rust warm-up.
Marcus: "I was showing the app off at a party. It's a hit. Pivot the whole business"
Alex rolls 1-1-1 = 3. Marcus: "bitch for the day numbers!!" - the earliest BITCH reference; the bot only implements it on 2025-06-23
Marcus responds to the bot's "go make tea baldy" line by linking the Guardian article "Calling a man bald is sexual harassment, employment tribunal rules"
Alex Williams posts the roadmap that defines the next six months of the bot: "Rerolls / Bitch/king for day features / fix timer". All three ship eventually.
Sasha: "what happens if we roll king/bitch but the feature is NYI?" Marcus: "it's enforced via shame"
Sasha rolls 18; Musa crowns him "King for the day" by hand. Alex: "the first king in the new kingdom?" The bot only automates KING on 2025-07-17.
Marcus, back from paternity leave: "the prevalence of 'ot' has increased massively since I've been on pat leave. what gives"
Stephen after an unbroken tie: "reroll ... make it do a reroll". Marcus: "the dice have spoken". Tie rerolls ship in June.
Tim asks for the bot to occasionally require a PHYSICAL dice roll instead - "The physical was fun occasionally". Marcus: "plz ignore this request". Musa: "will add it to the very long backlog"

Tea bot stops responding; Musa: "tea bot has zero downtime but i think you hit the rate limit for the slack api with your antics earlier". Stephen: "RIP teabot". Alex: "we'll have to roll dice like cave people"
Sasha proposes "lonely tea" for the no-takers case; the bot later adopts it for declined offers
Bot dead; Marcus spams "tttt botttttt / PLZZZZ". Alex: "teabot > nova ui"
Alex Williams: "bt - for when theres a bitch and you want tea" - the first sighting of the BITCH idea, which shipped ~4 months later
Stephen joins #t
Aatif Syed joins #t
Marcus joins #t
Musa, Jem, Stephen, Sasha and Tim all join #t within 21 seconds of each other
Alex Williams joins #t
Early bot had no tie-break reroll: equal totals were resolved by ordering alone. Rerolls appear from 2025-06-10.
TEA BOT GOES LIVE. First tracked round: stephen requests, musa loses. Join window 10s, brew timer 1 min (both later lengthened to 30s / 5 min).

promise mechanic: the bot refuses Sasha's fancy-tea preference - "Sorry Sasha, only standard tea is available. Please type 'promise' to promise that you will accept standard tea." Removed by 2025-06-10 ("I got rid of promise")
Teaderboard (stats tracking) added. The bot itself predates it - rounds run from at least 2025-06-02.
Bot ad-libs at Marcus: "ha, go make tea baldy"
Musa links src/main.rs of github.com/musahmad/tea-bot after Alex offers to add Slack tables
Bot briefly renders the Teaderboard as a monospaced markdown table (Alex Williams' PR); reverted within the hour
Musa: "im docking points for that one sorry". Marcus: "he's gone power mad"
Sasha: "wen will the dashboard be reversed?"

Bot switches from a plain "Dice roll results:" summary to animated per-die :dice-N: messages. Jem: "Woah these are some next generation graphics". Musa: "thanks i built a custom rendering engine from scratch"
Bot goes unresponsive; Marcus: "deadbot". Musa: "weird i didnt change anything"
Jem computes the odds of the same person rolling three-of-a-kind and then the bitch roll: 1 in 7776
Laurence Lewars joins #t
Alex Williams asks to convert the tea bot into a beer bot for the week; Sasha: "easy, just make it generic on beverage"
Eoin Devlin joins #t
Musa hand-edits the bot's stats JSON to credit an unregistered "ot"
Alex on the six-dice king bug: "took me 6 of the bloody things to get to 18". Sasha: "we need this bug fixed"
Aatif sets the #t channel topic to :teapot: and description to :teapot: :coffee:
Aatif links tea-bot issue #3
Alex Williams asks for a single-line Teaderboard sorted by teas-per-round ratio
Tim asks Musa for a "tt" command to start a tea timer
KING mechanic: rolling 6-6-6 (=18) makes you king for the day and exempt from making tea. Marcus is the one who triggers it here.
Alex Williams: "a t-bot token would be brilliant mumu" - the first mention of a TEA token, four and a half months before it shipped

The Teaderboard is WIPED. Pre-reset final standings (teas made): jem 82, musa 78, sasha 69, alex 53, stephen 48, marcus 39, tim 24, laurence 13. King counts alex 3, stephen 1, marcus 1; bitch sasha 1. Everything after this restarts from zero.
Aatif coins "teaderboard" ("teabot has the ~tea leaderboard~ teaderboard"); the bot's board is renamed within days
Musa links tea-bot commit f50b46717f692be488d391dec90308d6705e2b42 minutes after the six-dice bug
Marcus and Jem spam 30+ rt/t/tr/trt variants in ~15 seconds; the bot fires two overlapping tea rounds and interleaves their dice output
Tania Atyabi joins #t
Bot renames the stats board from "Tea Leaderboard" to "Teaderboard"
Laura joins #t
Martyn North joins #t - goes on to become the all-time teas-made leader
Martyn's "ot" did not register; he honoured the tea round manually
BITCH mechanic revealed: rolling 1-1-1 (=3) makes you "bitch for the day" and you must make ALL the teas. Musa is the only person ever to do it.
Megan Williams joins #t
pr <user> bot command in use (era 2)
tania appears on the Teaderboard (5 rounds, 0 teas made)
stats prints the Teaderboard on demand

Alexander Stepanov posts the RFC that becomes Era 3: on-chain TEA airdrop, sealed-bid auction, lowest bid makes tea, dice to break ties, pay/receive = own bid minus average of everyone else's, secondary TEA/USDT orderbook, points for holding
/bid command being tested in-channel (jem "/bid 2", marcus "/bid 1") four days before the bidding era starts
Marcus posts the TEA contract address 0x7eAb07a82f20C296aaC0025e93296EFce21D8bE1 in-channel
Round-start prompt example was "/t 5.5" (fractional bids allowed); later changed to "/t 5"
Musa asks everyone for their Arbitrum addresses to be added to the tea bot
Marcus walks the channel through ERC-20 approve() on arbiscan for contract 0x7eAb07a8..., spender 0x7ead7bff9c7edb076658be8dee4561af81427b57, amount max-uint256
Martyn: could you spend TEA on actions, e.g. 30 TEA to force someone to make you tea - "help whales liquidate"
Marcus posts a Uniswap TEA pool on Arbitrum - "premarket is live"; Sasha jokes about a 1% fee
Musa links tea-bot PR #6 (the bidding rewrite)
FIRST BIDDING ROUND. Era 2 (roll-only + stats board) ends, Era 3 (sealed bids + TEA currency) begins
Earliest rounds allowed FRACTIONAL bids (0.2, 0.4, 0.6) and printed explicit "Transfers to be made: A -> B: amount" lines
Musa: "Integers only" - fractional bids disabled
Musa added the "t" integration to the channel; channel description set to "test"
Settlement failed on-chain: "erc20: insufficient allowance" (first transfer failure)
Martyn: "looks like we all just bidding 0 from now on then / gameover" - the race to zero begins on day one
Early tiebreaks are inconsistent about whether high or low roll makes the tea (14:42 low roll lost; 14:46 high roll lost). Later rounds settle consistently on LOWEST roll makes the tea.
Marcus asks Musa for a fixed 3 TEA loser penalty split among participants; Sasha suggests a fixed per-person amount instead
Martyn bid 40 TEA in a 2-player round and lost all 40 to Musa. Martyn 93.5 -> 53.5, Musa 93.9 -> 133.9. Sasha: "where's price band protection?"
martyn rolled 6-6-6 = 18 (KING) in tiebreak; Martyn: "king status activated (manual)"
Amrit Sohal joined #t
stephen rolled 6-6-6 = 18 (KING) in a tiebreak reroll
Martyn: on a tied lowest bid all tied losers should lose their full bid, not a split share - "get some liquidity moving!"
Rad joined #t (also new to lo.tech)
Aatif opens tea-bot PR #7
Martyn opens tea-bot PR #8
round cancelled by Musa
:guinness: (Eoin Devlin) appears on the teaderboard with the 69.0 TEA seed but never plays; Sasha: "Eoin's TEA tokens should be burned". On-chain 0x1cd51346, seeded 2025-12-08, one tx ever
round cancelled by Musa
No tea rounds for ~11 days
Sasha argues the loser penalty should be fixed or 1x, not 2x - "wrong incentive to bid all your balance and screw someone over"
Musa opens tea-bot PR #10 (dice-based Loser Penalty); penalty line first appears in rounds from 2026-04-07
Musa states the payout formula: base payout = (average of all OTHER bids) - your own bid; the loser penalty is then taken from the loser and split evenly among the other participants
Musa bid 56 TEA (meant 5/6) - paid out 50.2 TEA: sasha +14.8, alex +14.8, martyn +13.5, stephen +7.2. Balance 125.7 -> 75.5
Bot stops posting per-player "X has joined the tea round" lines (present until ~2026-04-30 14:40)
